subject: Custom service guarantee exhibit — routing to Legal + Procurement
body:
-----Original Message-----
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acuhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Ruiz <samantha.ruiz@acuhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA exhibit — two asks from procurement

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement had two quick asks before Legal starts redlining:

1) We need a precise uptime definition — is it per-region or global? Our risk team wants the metric to be per-region as they rely on local failover.
2) Latency tiers — they asked for an attenuation credit structure if 95th pct > X ms for production model endpoints.

Can you share a short exhibit we can hang off the MSA illustrating the metric, measurement windows, and credit schedule? Samantha is copied and will coordinate procurement timeline.

Liam
Director, IT Procurement
AcuHealth

-----Reply-----
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acuhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA exhibit — two asks from procurement

Hi Liam — great questions. Short answers up front:
- Uptime measurement: per-region by default (we can also do global).
- Latency credits: we can propose a 95th percentile credit ladder tied to per-route SLOs; will map to token throttling windows and traffic tiers.

I'm attaching a first-pass exhibit that lays out: measurement windows (UTC daily), per-region availability calc, and a three-tier credit schedule for 95th-ms bands. Kimberly (Legal) and Karthik (Customer Ops) are on copy to help with language and evidence requirements.

Next steps I propose:
1) Kimberly to review legal language and flag clauses that need enterprise escalations.
2) Karthik to attach the telemetry/ops requirements we need during onboarding (SLO tests, retention, access for evidence).
3) Liam/Samantha to confirm the target latencies and the procurement timeline for DocuSign.

If this looks reasonable I'll move to a redline draft for AcuHealth Legal.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RDW_AcuHealth_SLA_Exhibit_draft_v1.pdf (exhibit draft)

-----Forwarded message-----
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acuhealth.com>; Samantha Ruiz <samantha.ruiz@acuhealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jul 2028 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: RDW proposed language + evidence items

Hello Liam / Samantha,

Attaching redlines and a brief evidence matrix. A few callouts before you dive in:

- We explain uptime as per-region and include a global-failover footnote that describes the behavior when a region experiences a partial outage. That should satisfy your risk team while keeping the metric operationally coherent.
- For latency credits we proposed bands at >95ms, >200ms and >500ms (95th pct) with scaled credits tied to monthly token spend rather than flat amounts; finance prefers this because it aligns commercial exposure to usage.
- Evidence: we require a 30-day telemetry export, and a timestamped sampling of KV cache hit-rates for defendants of prefix caching during incidents. We can provide these via an S3 share and a limited telemetry view in the Console once onboarding is complete.

Open items for Legal: indemnity linkage for degraded-mode fallbacks and explicit limits on the scope of credits in partial-degradation events.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Transactions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RDW_AcuHealth_SLA_Exhibit_redlines_from_AcuLegal.pdf; procurement-matrix.xlsx

-----Reply (AcuHealth Legal)-----
From: AcuHealth Legal <legal@acuhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acuhealth.com>, Samantha Ruiz <samantha.ruiz@acuhealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jul 2028 11:15:00 -0500
Subject: Re: RDW proposed language + evidence items

Kimberly — thanks for the quick turn. A few notes from our counsel:

1) We need the uptime calc made explicit in the exhibit (sample equation). Our tech reviewer wants the ability to recompute the metric from exported telemetry without ambiguity.
2) The credit ladder is acceptable but we need a maximum liability cap per incident/month (we suggested 20% of the monthly subscription line item).
3) Evidence access: AcuHealth requests continuous access to the telemetry export (not just 30-day snapshots) for the first 90 days of production to verify initial SLA compliance. After that, periodic exports will be fine.

Please provide a revised exhibit with the equation and proposed liability cap so Legal can give a final sign-off.

Regards,
AcuHealth Legal

-----Reply (Sean) to AcuHealth Legal + internal team-----
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: AcuHealth Legal <legal@acuhealth.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acuhealth.com>, Samantha Ruiz <samantha.ruiz@acuhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jul 2028 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RDW proposed language + evidence items

Thanks — understood. Kimberly and I aligned offline: we can include a clear uptime formula (percentage = 1 - (sum_downtime_seconds / total_seconds_in_window) * 100) in the exhibit and publish a canonical telemetry export schema for recomputation.

On the liability cap: Redwood's standard is to tie credits to monthly subscription charges; we can accept a negotiated per-month cap but risk/finance will need to sign off on the percentage. Karthik, can you confirm if a 20% per-month cap is feasible for this enterprise slot or if we should propose 15%?

On continuous telemetry access: operationally we can provide a streaming export feed into a customer S3 (90-day window retention) for the first 90 days, then switch to scheduled exports. We'll surface the export spec in the Drive link.

If AcuHealth is ok with those three items today, we will: (1) circulate the exhibit with the equation and cap noted, (2) route to DocuSign with procurement's target dates, and (3) start the telemetry export setup during onboarding.

Best,
Sean

-----Final reply (Samantha, AcuHealth Procurement)-----
From: Samantha Ruiz <samantha.ruiz@acuhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acuhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, AcuHealth Legal <legal@acuhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jul 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Custom service guarantee exhibit — routing to Legal + Procurement

Thanks everyone — this is helpful. Procurement can accept the following as the path forward: 
- Redwood to issue revised exhibit with explicit equation and proposed 15% and 20% cap options by end of day Friday (7/26).
- AcuHealth Legal to review liability cap options and confirm preferred %; procurement to target execution by 8/02.
- Redwood to stand up the 90-day streaming telemetry export during onboarding; procurement will provide S3 destination details once DocuSign is completed.

Please put the revised exhibit in the Drive link and flag the HubSpot deal when the envelope is created.

Samantha Ruiz
Senior Manager, Strategic Sourcing
AcuHealth

Attachments referenced in thread: RDW_AcuHealth_SLA_Exhibit_draft_v1.pdf; RDW_AcuHealth_SLA_Exhibit_redlines_from_AcuLegal.pdf; procurement-matrix.xlsx
